excerpt: ShipBob runs e-commerce fulfilment for online brands: storage, pick and pack, shipping and returns across its warehouse network. Pricing is quote-based.
content:
ShipBob is a Chicago company that handles order fulfilment for e-commerce brands. A brand sends its inventory to ShipBob's fulfilment centres; when a customer orders from the brand's online store or marketplace channel, ShipBob picks, packs and ships the order and handles returns. Its website pitches fast delivery promises such as two-day shipping, branded unboxing, omnichannel and international fulfilment, and spreading inventory across its network to cut shipping costs and times. It also offers B2B and wholesale fulfilment, kitting, and its own warehouse management system for brands that run their own warehouses, plus integrations with e-commerce platforms and ERPs such as NetSuite.

Dhruv Saxena (CEO) and Divey Gulati founded ShipBob. When it raised its Series E in 2021, TechCrunch reported that it worked with some 5,000 e-commerce businesses and ran around 20 fulfilment centres across the US, Canada, Europe and Australia, with plans for 10 more.

Funding

On 29 June 2021 ShipBob announced a $200 million Series E led by Bain Capital Ventures, valuing it at more than $1 billion, double its Series D valuation from September 2020. Built In Chicago reported that SoftBank, Menlo Ventures and Hyde Park Venture Partners also took part.

Pricing

ShipBob does not publish rates. Its pricing page says all quotes are customised and lists the standard fee types: receiving, storage, pick and pack, shipping (which depends on weight, size, destination and speed) and a flat fee per return. It says its software and integrations are free for customers and that standard boxes, mailers and labels are included at no charge, while kitting and B2B/EDI work are quoted separately.

Who it suits

ShipBob suits direct-to-consumer brands that have outgrown packing orders themselves and want a network of warehouses without running one. Very small sellers with only a few orders a month may find a quote-based 3PL more than they need.

We have not used ShipBob. This page is based on ShipBob's website and pricing page (checked 15 October 2026), TechCrunch and Built In Chicago.
